title: Bars and 4/4 time
summary: Find out what the two numbers at the start mean and count bars of 4.
usSummary: Find out what the two numbers at the start mean and count measures of 4.

hook.text: Before a band starts, the drummer clicks the sticks and counts out loud: 1, 2, 3, 4. Why four? Press play and count along with this tune, one number for every tick. Where does your count go back to 1?

explore.text: Your turn. Tap the pad on every note and count out loud: 1, 2, 3, 4. Each time a new [[bar|bar]] begins, start again at 1. Keep counting through the long notes.
explore.goal: Tap all 4 [[bar|bars]] while you count 1, 2, 3, 4 in every one.

cards.text: You counted 1, 2, 3, 4 in every [[bar|bar]], then started again. The two numbers at the start of the music tell you to do that. They are the [[time-signature|time signature]]. This one says 4/4.

The top number is how many beats are in each [[bar|bar]]: 4. The bottom number says which note gets one beat. A bottom 4 means each beat is a [[crotchet|crotchet]]. So a [[bar|bar]] of 4/4 holds 4 [[crotchet|crotchets]], or the same length made with [[minim|minims]].
Music in 4/4 is in [[quadruple-time|quadruple time]]. Count 1, 2, 3, 4 and lean on beat 1: it is the strongest. Beat 3 is the next strongest. Beats 2 and 4 are light.

alternative.text: Think of a bus with 4 seats. A [[crotchet|crotchet]] takes 1 seat and a [[minim|minim]] takes 2. The 4/4 says the bus has 4 seats. A [[bar|bar]] is full when every seat is taken: nobody standing, no seat empty. Here: 1 + 1 + 2 = 4.

points: Count 1, 2, 3, 4 and start again at 1 in each new [[bar|bar]]. In 4/4 every [[bar|bar]] holds 4 beats.
The [[time-signature|time signature]] is the two numbers at the start. The top number is the beats in each [[bar|bar]]; the bottom 4 means each beat is a [[crotchet|crotchet]].
